question: According to the standard morphological classification of anaemia, which MCV range correctly identifies normocytic anaemia in an adult?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: An MCV below 70 fL indicates microcytosis, not normocytosis. This range is seen in severe iron deficiency or thalassaemia major.
Correct. The normocytic range is conventionally 80–100 fL. Anaemia within this range includes aplastic anaemia, acute haemorrhage, and anaemia of chronic disease.
The 70–79 fL range is borderline microcytic. While some texts place the lower limit at 80 fL, values in this range warrant iron studies and may represent mild IDA or thalassaemia trait.
MCV > 100 fL defines macrocytosis. Causes include B12/folate deficiency (megaloblastic), liver disease, hypothyroidism, and myelodysplastic syndrome.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the MCV thresholds: microcytic <80 fL, normocytic 80–100 fL, macrocytic >100 fL. These form the backbone of the morphological classification.
Well done. The normocytic range (80–100 fL) is the starting point for the two-axis morphological-kinetic classification of anaemia.
